title: Docker CLI — Run Lifecycle, System Commands, Inspection
subtitle: The most interview-critical Docker CLI commands and their flags

nodes.label:
docker run
Pull image if missing
Create + start container
Attach / detach (-d)

docker exec
Run cmd in running container
-it for interactive shell
Same namespaces

docker stop / kill
SIGTERM → 10s grace → SIGKILL
kill -s SIGKILL skips grace

docker inspect
Full JSON — IPs, mounts, env
docker logs --tail --follow
docker stats (live cgroup)

panels.title: Essential CLI patterns
panels.body:
# Run with restart + resource limits + read-only FS
docker run -d --name api \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --memory 512m --cpus 1.5 \
  --read-only --tmpfs /tmp \
  --cap-drop ALL --cap-add NET_BIND_SERVICE \
  -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 \
  myapp:v1.2.3

# Debug a running container
docker exec -it api sh
docker logs api --tail 100 --follow
docker inspect api | jq '.[0].NetworkSettings.Networks'

# Live resource usage
docker stats              # all containers
docker stats api --no-stream   # one-shot snapshot

# Disk usage audit
docker system df -v       # detailed breakdown
docker system prune -af --volumes   # nuclear cleanup

# Copy files in/out without a volume
docker cp api:/app/logs/error.log ./error.log
docker cp ./config.json api:/app/config.json

# Inspect image layers
docker image history myapp:v1.2.3 --no-trunc
docker inspect myapp:v1.2.3 | jq '.[0].RootFS.Layers | length'

panels.title: CLI traps interviewers test
panels.body:
docker stop vs docker kill:
  stop sends SIGTERM, waits --time seconds (default 10), then SIGKILL.
  kill sends SIGKILL immediately by default — no graceful shutdown.
  Prefer stop unless the container is frozen/unresponsive.

docker run --rm vs named container:
  --rm auto-removes the container on exit. Named containers ('-n foo')
  persist and can be restarted. '--rm' is incompatible with '--restart'.

docker exec vs docker run:
  exec runs inside a running container's existing namespaces.
  run starts a NEW container from the image — a completely separate process.
  'docker exec' on a crashed container returns: 'Error — container not running'.

docker logs only works with json-file or journald log drivers.
With fluentd/awslogs drivers, docker logs returns an error — logs
were already shipped to the external system.

docker system prune removes:
  stopped containers, dangling images, unused networks, build cache.
  --volumes ALSO removes unnamed (anonymous) volumes — dangerous.
  Named volumes are NEVER removed without explicit 'docker volume rm'.

panels.title: restart policies
pros: unless-stopped: restarts after crashes AND after daemon restart — best for production services
on-failure:3: restarts only on non-zero exit up to 3 times — prevents infinite loops on config errors
cons: always: also restarts containers you manually stopped with 'docker stop' after daemon restart — often surprising
no (default): container never restarts; process crashes mean permanent downtime without an external supervisor
